about: The egg pictures, described for the Brobots (operator 2026-10-16: "generate descriptions for brobots, like a list of value points, to use in their responses in live runs * not generate per live run"). Made at Wire-Pod's start only for a picture with no points or one that changed (md5); edit points by hand freely - they stay until the picture itself changes. gopod_picture_describe.go. 2026-10-16: the first points from the vision model were mostly wrong ("BROOOTS CHOCOLATE BRONBO", a Sims 4 page, keychains, toy trains); each picture's points were then written by hand from the picture itself.

points: Brobots Chocolate Bingo, Card No. 01: a 4 x 4 quick game.
Cover any full line of 4, then shout "BROBOTS!"
Its squares are robot-chocolate names like Choco Servo, Mousse Motor, Brownie Byte, Cookie Circuit and Nougat Nugget, with a FREE Brobots square.
Every card in the kit is unique; print one per player, and it reads clean in black and white.
The cover of Chocolate Bingo, a Brobots CRUSHN8R CREW'D kit: the all-ages game kit and recipe pack.
It shows a 5 x 5 card of robot-chocolate names like Bonbon Beacon, Wafer Widget and Fudge Fuse, with a FREE Brobots square in the middle.
Two lanes: Kids' Lane and Adults' Lane.
Print at home, plays in black and white, and zero real brands - all Brobots.
The Recipe Pack: make the treats on the cards for real - two lanes, one chocolate family (Kids' Lane).
Brobots Chocolate Cookies with Nuts!!: makes 24 cookies in 25 minutes, easy.
Brobots Fudge Bolt Squares: makes 16 squares in 15 minutes plus chilling, no-bake.
A grown-up handles the oven and anything hot.
A black and white qr code image with a square in the center of it.
Doc's Answer Key, "The Answers. Obviously.": the same problems, over-the-top correct.
One Doc line per problem names Pip's exact error - a miss is a miss, no credit for near.
The problems are factors: 12 = 2 x 6 or 3 x 4, the factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 18, and 24 = 6 x 4.
The Doc & Pip Math Workbook concept pitch board, with Doc (orange) and Pip (teal) as cartoon robots.
Pip works it out - confidently, charmingly wrong. Doc's key names the mistake and fixes it.
Pip's mistakes are the ones real learners actually make; error on the left, correction on the right.
Its first section is Pip's Clueless Workbook.
Gangster Granny: Brobot 0's sweet, adorable, gangster granny - a 93-year-old who helped him when it counted.
A cheeky little granny with white curls, big blue eyes, long lashes, rosy cheeks and a sly smirk.
Her hat: a black hat covered in sparkling rhinestones, a silver dollar sign on the side, white roses and silver leaves on top.
She's dressed to the nines: a pink fur coat with white fur cuffs, a white shirt and a big sparkly silver bow tie.
Bling everywhere: dangling diamond earrings, stacked diamond bracelets on both wrists, a big diamond ring.
In her hand, a sparkly rhinestone cigarette with a curl of smoke - gangster style.
The GOPOD rig laid out on a couch: two Vector robots on their chargers - the Brobots.
Two Cozmo robots, a microphone, a numpad, a mobile hotspot and a Coral Edge TPU stick.
The brain: a Seeed Studio box with two antennas - the Jetson that runs GOPOD locally.
A full pizza box of food-shaped Hot Wheels cars, lined up in rows on orange track.
Donut cars, blue frosted cars, chocolate cupcake cars, chocolate cake-slice cars and rows of pink cake-slice cars.
A pink donut truck and donut shop cars at the top - already bought, already sorted, for a GOPOD birthday.
More food-shaped Hot Wheels cars in the pizza box, in rows on orange track.
Teal donut cars, pink and blue cake-slice cars, chocolate cake slices, and rows of white whipped-cream cars with grape, cherry, lime and orange flavours.
Party food on wheels - the table dressing and the prize for a GOPOD birthday.
